question_text: An Indigenous Cultural Community (ICC) in Mindanao claims ancestral domain over a forest area that a mining company has been granted a permit to explore. Under RA 8371 (Indigenous Peoples Rights Act or IPRA), what is the legal status of the ICC's claim?

options.text: The ICC has no claim because the mining permit was issued by the government.
The ICC has a right to ancestral domain, and the mining permit cannot be valid without their free, prior, and informed consent (FPIC).
The ICC can only claim ownership of the land they currently occupy, not the entire forest area.
The ICC's claim is subject to the mining permit, which takes precedence under the Mining Act.
